newsitem.title: RUSSIA: UES says may not meet low industry rate goal in 97.
newsitem.headline: UES says may not meet low industry rate goal in 97.

text.p: Russian national electric company UES may not meet its plan to cut electricity rates to industry by 13 percent this year, the chief of the company's economy department said on Wednesday.
"That is RAO UES's goal, but it may not be in our power," Sergei Obratsov said in an interview.
Russian First Deputy Prime Minister Boris Nemtsov quoted UES's president on Tuesday as saying UES planned to cut rates to manufacturers by 13 percent this year.
Russian electricity rates to industry are relatively expensive and the government has made lowering them a key component of its plans to reform UES and stimulate Russian industry.

RAO Yedinaya Energeticheskaya Sistema Rossii (UES) is Russia's biggest company by sales and a natural monopoly which has no competitor and is largely regulated. Nemtsov has criticised management for leading UES into a payments crisis.
But Obratsov said UES was not in full control of pricing policy, adding that federal and regional regulators fixed electricity rates.
